2.2 Surrogate likelihood for terminal-feedback optimization of MDLMs
[id=S2.SS2.p1.1] Masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) generate text by iteratively refining a partially-masked sequence, unmasking tokens in an arbitrary order.
This makes the exact sequence likelihood log⁡πθ​(o∣q)\log\pi_{\theta}(o\!\mid\!q) intractable, which prevents directly applying standard terminal-feedback objectives such as § 2.1.
To enable terminal-feedback policy optimization for MDLMs, Zhao et al. (2025b) introduces a tractable surrogate likelihood π~θ\tilde{\pi}_{\theta} (yielding an MDLM instantiation often referred to as diffu-GRPO).
[id=S2.SS2.p2.1] Given a prompt–completion pair (q,o)(q,o), we sample a random prompt-masking pattern mm to obtain a corrupted prompt q(m)q^{(m)}.
We then form a fully masked completion o~\tilde{o}, run a single denoising step to obtain per-position token distributions
pθ(⋅∣q(m),o~)p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q^{(m)},\tilde{o}), and define the surrogate log-probability
[id=S2.E1]
log⁡π~θ​(o∣q)=𝔼m​[∑j=1|o|log⁡pθ​(oj∣q(m),o~)].\log\tilde{\pi}_{\theta}(o\mid q)\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{m}\!\left[\;\sum_{j=1}^{|o|}\log p_{\theta}\!\bigl(o_{j}\mid q^{(m)},\tilde{o}\bigr)\;\right].
(1)
[id=S2.SS2.p2.2] In terminal-feedback MDLM policy optimization, π~θ\tilde{\pi}_{\theta} replaces πθ\pi_{\theta} inside likelihood ratios and KL terms, allowing MDLMs to be trained as conditional policies from scalar rewards on final completions.
[id=S2.SS3]
2.3 Rethinking MDLM decision points for RL
[id=S2.SS3.p1.1] In an episodic MDP, the policy gradient theorem (Williams, 1992; Sutton et al., 1999) states that for a stochastic policy πθ​(at∣st)\pi_{\theta}(a_{t}\mid s_{t}),
[id=S2.Ex2]
∇θJ​(θ)=𝔼⁡[∑t∇θ​log​πθ​(at∣st)​Gt],\nabla_{\theta}J(\theta)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{t}\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi_{\theta}(a_{t}\mid s_{t})\,G_{t}\right],
[id=S2.SS3.p1.2] where sts_{t} and ata_{t} are the state and action, and GtG_{t} denotes the return from step tt.
Each decision (st,at)(s_{t},a_{t}) contributes an explicit term
∇θ​log​πθ​(at∣st)​Gt\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi_{\theta}(a_{t}\!\mid\!s_{t})\,G_{t}.
This decomposition enables fine-grained credit assignment across steps.
[id=S2.SS3.p2.1] Most RL formulations for LMs (autoregressive or diffusion) collapse decoding to a terminal-reward bandit, where reward evaluation and gradient attribution are both driven by the final completion (Shao et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2025b).
MDLMs, however, provide an anytime completion interface: at an intermediate masked state, a single forward pass yields logits for all masked positions.
Hence we can view the masked sequence as the state sts_{t} and its mask fillings as the action ata_{t}; filling deterministically yields a completion to score with the same terminal reward, and cached logits enable multiple same-state counterfactual completions without additional rollout forward passes.
This state–action view motivates our diffusion-state policy optimization in §3.
